subject.title: Browser: support blocked URL paths / domain denylist

question: Should OpenClaw add a public browser navigation deny/warn policy, and what traffic classes must it cover across top-level navigation, redirects, subframes, subresources, downloads, and proxy-routed profiles?
rationale: The request creates an operator-trusted browser security/config surface, so automation should not choose denylist, warnlist, or bundled default-list semantics without maintainer security intent.

options.title: Design browser policy contract first
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define enforceable denylist semantics separately from advisory bot-block warnings before implementation.

options.title: Fold into broader egress policy
options.body: Let https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/39685 own this only if the design explicitly includes browser navigation and browser-specific traffic classes.

options.title: Advisory hints only
options.body: Avoid an enforceable browser denylist for now and provide only best-effort warnings for known bot-blocked sites.

recommendation.title: Design browser policy contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers define enforceable denylist semantics separately from advisory bot-block warnings before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest current-history signal across browser SSRF config, navigation policy, docs, and recent adjacent fixes.
